concept.name: Setup quality
concept.definition: A grade of how well a specific trade opportunity matches the trader's validated setups and current market conditions - in proprietary-trading practice expressed as tiers (A/B/C) that gate size and frequency. It operationalizes selectivity: capital concentrates on the highest-quality instances of proven patterns.
concept.intuition: Not every valid-looking pattern deserves the same money; an A-setup in the right market is a different bet from a marginal lookalike.
concept.mechanics: Playbook setups are scored before entry against confluence factors (trend, level, volume, catalyst, time of day, the setup's recent tracked performance); the grade determines whether to trade and how much to risk. Bellafiore's SMB framework ties grade to conviction and size, and grades are audited in daily review.
concept.failure_modes: Grades drift under emotion: after losses everything looks like a C, after wins everything looks like an A. Grading without historical per-setup expectancy data is subjective relabeling, not measurement.
concept.misconceptions: Quality is a property of the setup-context match, not of how confident or excited the trader feels. Skipping B and C setups is not cowardice - it is how expectancy is protected when edges are thin.
concept.example: A pullback-to-VWAP long in a strong trend after earnings grades A and gets full size; the same pattern in a choppy midday tape grades C and is skipped.

citations.source: Mike Bellafiore, One Good Trade: Inside the Highly Competitive World of Proprietary Trading (Wiley, 2010) - publisher page
